body:
Ugh.

So the only reason this line exists at all is because the default `bash` on MacOS is from 2007, and doesn't support sourcing from process redirection. (if you follow the link in the comment above that line, you'll find an SO question dealing with this problem).

I think if you use any semi-modern version of bash, (I think the 4.x release series will work, but not 100% sure on that), you can use a line that's more-or-less identical to the one in the zsh init.

I'd really love to just drop support for a piece of software that's older than some high schoolers right now, but unfortunately, 3.2 is the default version on MacOS, and it's unlikely to ever be version-bumped because of GPLv3.

One solution we can look into is trying to parse the bash version string--if it's newer than whatever version we need to do procsub with `source`, we can just do that, otherwise we'd have to use the old version. We'd need to determine what the earliest version of bash is that can support that though.
